newsitem.title: USA: S&P says may take rating action on Northeast.
newsitem.headline: S&P says may take rating action on Northeast.

text.p: A Standard & Poor's official said Monday his investors' service will decide whether to downgrade the credit ratings of Northeast Utilities and its utility subsidiaries later this week.
"Clearly, the recent New Hampshire issuance of the final rules for restructuring (its electric industry) is negative," said Raymond Leung, associate director at Standard & Poor's.
"We'll take a look at the ratings and take appropriate action," Leung told Reuters.
"We've had (Northeast) on credit watch for some time now."

Earlier Monday, Moody's Investor Service downgraded the credit ratings of Northeast, along with those of two of its utility subsidiaries, Public Service Co of New Hampshire and North Atlantic Energy Corp.

Moody's said the downgrades reflected increased regulatory and financial uncertainty stemming from the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission's decision on Feb 28 regarding interim stranded cost recovery for Public Service New Hampshire, the state's largest electric utility.
Northeast said Monday it was filing suit in U.S. District Court in Concord, N.H., against the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission, challenging its restructuring order.

Leung said Northeast faced serious problems over proposed deregulation in New Hampshire, as well as continuing woes related to the shutdown of its three Millstone nuclear plants in Waterford, Conn., since March 1996.
He said the nuclear problems have already cost the company close to $600 million. "The nuclear woes will continue to challenge the company in the face of a deregulating environment," Leung said.
He said that because some overlap within Northeast's management and operations, any problems in one business could potentially affect the ratings of all its businesses.
Leung said that because of the deregulation trend sweeping the country, "At this point, it's a bad time to have a significant portion of your generating assets not performing."

"That has essentially drained away significant wells of cash flow from the company. Until they can get these plants up and running, they will continue to be a drag. Now the movement of restructuring has accelerated within their states, and that has been a concern of ours for some time."
Northeast has said it plans to have all three Millstone plants ready for restart by early 1998.
At present, Standard & Poor's rates Public Service New Hampshire at BB+ for senior secured debt.
Its senior rating for North Atlantic Energy Corp is BB; Western Massachusetts Electric Company is BBB minus; Connecticut Light and Power is BBB minus; and Northeast Utilities is BB.
Northeast's stock was down 3/4 to 9-5/8 on volume of 1.79 million shares late on Monday.
